lesson_title: The City of Gold Fights Back
hook_text: In 1886 it was a camp of tents. By 1911, nearly a quarter of a million people lived there, and many of them were fighting back.
clip_script: Johannesburg grows overnight: miners, traders, washermen, families from everywhere. The rich build mansions on the Parktown ridge. The poor crowd into Brickfields and Vrededorp. Black miners can't vote or form unions, so they resist quietly: they desert, they warn friends about bad mines, they go slow. In 1913, white miners strike and soldiers fire into a crowd. At the same time, nine thousand black miners strike too, and are forced back at gunpoint. In 1904, after plague, the council burns a location and moves black residents to Klipspruit, the start of Soweto. A city built on gold, divided by race, and full of people who refused to stay silent.
visual_style: A whiteboard city drawing itself from tents to buildings, with a ridge of mansions, mine dumps, compounds and a location on the edge, then figures walking away from a mine, and a crowd on a street.
pacing: Fast growth, slower over the strike, ending on a wide view of the city.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to explore resistance in the city of gold.
